question: Which among the following organic compounds is saturated?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bromopropane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Saturated hydrocarbons** are compounds where all the carbon-carbon bonds are single bonds. These are also known as alkanes or their derivatives.
 
• **Bromopropane** is a derivative of propane, which is an alkane. In bromopropane, one hydrogen atom in propane is replaced by a bromine atom, but the structure remains saturated as it contains only single bonds between carbon atoms.
 
• **Propyne** contains a triple bond between two carbon atoms, making it an unsaturated compound. Hence, it is not saturated.
 
• **2-Bromopropene** contains a double bond between two carbon atoms, which also makes it unsaturated.
 
• **Propene** contains a double bond between two carbon atoms, classifying it as an unsaturated compound.
 
• Therefore, among the given options, **Bromopropane** is the only saturated compound because it contains only single bonds between carbon atoms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Saturated Hydrocarbons:**

 
 
• Saturated hydrocarbons are also known as alkanes. The general formula for alkanes is CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.
 
• They are characterized by single covalent bonds between carbon atoms, which makes them relatively less reactive compared to unsaturated hydrocarbons.
 
• Examples include methane (CH₄), ethane (C₂H₆), and propane (C₃H₈).
 
• Saturated hydrocarbons undergo substitution reactions rather than addition reactions due to the absence of multiple bonds.
 
 
 
• **Unsaturated Hydrocarbons:**
 
 
• Unsaturated hydrocarbons include alkenes and alkynes. Alkenes have at least one double bond (general formula: CₙH₂ₙ), while alkynes have at least one triple bond (general formula: CₙH₂ₙ₋₂).
 
• They are more reactive due to the presence of double or triple bonds, which can participate in addition reactions.
 
• Examples include ethene (C₂H₄), propene (C₃H₆), and ethyne (C₂H₂).
 
 
 
• **Functional Groups and Saturation:**
 
 
• The presence of functional groups (like bromine in bromopropane) does not affect the saturation of a hydrocarbon as long as the carbon-carbon bonds remain single.
 
• For example, bromopropane is saturated despite the presence of a bromine atom because its carbon backbone contains only single bonds.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Saturated Compounds:**
 
 
• Saturated hydrocarbons like alkanes are widely used as fuels, such as propane and butane in LPG (Liquefied Petroleum Gas).
 
• They are also used as solvents and in the production of various chemicals in the petrochemical industry.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Bromopropane:**

 
 
• It is a saturated organic compound with the formula C₃H₇Br.
 
• It is used as a solvent, especially in degreasing and cleaning applications.
 
• Bromopropane is also employed in the synthesis of pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals.
 
 
 
• **Propyne:**
 
 
• Propyne (C₃H₄) is an alkyne with a triple bond and is used as a fuel and in organic synthesis.
 
 
 
• **2-Bromopropene:**
 
 
• It contains a double bond and is classified as an alkene derivative. It is used in organic synthesis.
 
 
 
• **Propene:**
 
 
• Propene (C₃H₆) is an unsaturated hydrocarbon (alkene) used in the production of polypropylene and other chemicals.
